summary: CursorHide may leave the cursor invisible on the Windows security screen; verify desktop transitions before changing cursor restoration.
title: CursorHide hides mouse cursor when going to lock view (control + alt + del).
author: gregongoing

judgment.rationale: The report specifies CursorHide and the Ctrl+Alt+Del transition; the exact hidden-state trigger and secure-desktop behavior still need verification.
evidence: Reporter uses PowerToys 0.102.3101, describes the Ctrl+Alt+Del screen, and attaches a report ZIP.
SystemCursorHider::Hide replaces system cursor shapes with transparent cursors; the worker restores them on show or shutdown.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the desktop transition and cursor restoration

fix_assessment.rationale: System cursor replacement is a plausible contributor, but the transition and safe restore mechanism need verification before a fix is selected.

proposed_fixes.title: Restore cursor visibility around a confirmed secure-desktop transition
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: transparent system cursors remain active when the input desktop changes; the report does not establish the pre-transition hide state or mechanism.
plan: Compare cursor visibility and the worker's hide state before and after the security desktop transition.
If system cursor replacement causes the failure, restore the configured cursors at a reliable desktop-transition boundary without interfering with secure-desktop input.
On return, reconcile the worker's state before resuming the configured hide behavior; cover restore failures and normal shutdown.
verification: The security screen has a visible pointer after both hidden and visible pre-transition states.
Configured cursor schemes, ordinary hide/show behavior and shutdown restoration continue to work.

confidence.rationale: SetSystemCursor replaces cursor shapes, but persistence across this desktop transition and the trigger remain unconfirmed.

issue_context.summary: CursorHide may leave the cursor invisible on the Ctrl+Alt+Del security screen.
known_information: PowerToys 0.102.3101 installed through auto-update; reporter describes Ctrl+Alt+Del with CursorHide enabled.
The attached report records hide-on-typing enabled and hide-on-idle disabled.
inferences: Transparent cursor replacement may remain in effect across the desktop switch; this is not yet demonstrated.
issue_context.analysis: The attachment records hide-on-typing enabled and idle hiding disabled, but does not establish whether the pointer was hidden immediately before entering the security screen.
initial_investigation: SystemCursorHider.h replaces system cursor shapes via SetSystemCursor and restores them using SPI_SETCURSORS; AutoHideCursorWorker.cpp uses low-level input hooks, a timer, and restores on shutdown.
No covering PR found in a focused search for Auto Hide Cursor desktop work.
Inspected the attached report's CursorHide settings and relevant logs.

actions.label: Test cursor visibility across Ctrl+Alt+Del
actions.note: Compare hidden and visible pre-transition states before choosing a fix.

reproduce.title: Check CursorHide on the Windows security screen
prerequisites: Use a disposable Windows VM or dedicated test device with CursorHide enabled.
setup: Enable hide-on-typing and disable hide-on-idle as in the attached settings; keep a keyboard available to return from the security screen.
steps: Type to let CursorHide hide the pointer, then press Ctrl+Alt+Del and move the mouse on the security screen.
Return to the desktop and verify cursor restoration. Repeat after restoring the pointer before Ctrl+Alt+Del.
reproduce.expected_result: The cursor is visible and usable on the security screen and the configured cursor returns on the normal desktop.
